co_jamcrack_spire.blurb: A big, wide flatiron in the southern Flatirons above Boulder, with ten routes that are mostly trad plus a single top rope. The grades lean toward 5.9 and 5.10, with a couple of easy lines and one 5.11 for the strong. The west face holds the best crack climbing, while the east face is lower angle and reaches the top in several pitches. It sees few visitors compared with its famous neighbours, so expect quiet, but that also means loose rock and less-travelled approaches deserve care. Descents involve tree rappels, and extra webbing helps for replacing worn slings.

co_third_advisor.blurb: The southernmost of the three Advisors in the Flatirons above Boulder, holding ten trad routes on roughly 600 feet of broken, fractured rock. Grades run from third-class scrambling up to 5.10, mostly in the 5.8 and 5.9 range. Chimneys, brushy gullies and patches of poorer rock separate the better cracks, and some newer lines on the north face are decent. Route-finding is vague, and the base can be hard to recognise on arrival. Expect a bushwhacking, adventure-style outing rather than a polished crag, with a scramble down afterward.

co_moss_man.blurb: A small bouldering spot in Clear Creek Canyon near Golden, made up of just a couple of boulders and ten problems. It is a hard-leaning venue: most problems sit around V10, with a V5 at the easy end, a few in the V12 range and one V13 at the top. Strong boulderers will find a handful of well-known lines here, while those working up from lower grades will find little. The boulders sit a short walk up the hillside across the road from the creek.

co_teenage_wasteland.blurb: A slabby granite area tucked behind the Super Slab at Hartman Rocks near Gunnison, with ten routes mixing sport and trad, seven of them bolted. Difficulty runs from an easy 5.5 or so to a single 5.11, with most lines in the 5.8 to 5.10 band, so it suits climbers stepping up from beginner terrain as well as those wanting steady mid-grade slab. Most routes earn a decent star rating. The walk is brief, but you leave the bike track and pass through a notch to reach the slabs.

co_fruita_canyon.blurb: The first canyon you meet after entering Colorado National Monument from the west entrance, with a handful of routes close to the road. Of ten listed, seven are trad and three are aid, graded from 5.9 to 5.11, so there is nothing for true beginners. This is soft desert sandstone, and the rock can be loose and dirty, giving plenty of adventure for each pitch. The sandstone is fragile when wet, so let it dry fully before you climb.

co_tutorial_rock.blurb: A single block-like boulder on Flagstaff Mountain just west of Boulder, and the first one you reach on the trail. Its ten problems run from VB-V0 warm-ups up to a V8 traverse, with plenty in the V0 to V3 range. The faces are short and sharp, featuring slopers, rails and cobbles, with generally safe landings that suit beginners. Several traverses share their opening moves and diverge near the end. It works well for a quick session rather than a full day.
